pairs.why: A is a painted, grounded 3/4 coffin with a slightly open lid and soft wood shading, like the real cards; B is a flat, smooth orange slab standing on its end and reads as plastic.
A's thick, smooth, soft rope coil matches the chunky, clean finish of the scarf and fan; B's thin, finely twisted rope is the texture-heavy look the lessons rejected.
A has the bright, saturated colors and clean soft-lit shapes of the graduation cap; B's dull brownish felt finish is more muted and realistic than the real cards.
B's chunkier, smoother rope with a soft ground shadow sits closer to the real cards' clean finish; A's thin, detailed twist is too texture-heavy.
A's full wreath, big bow and wood-grain frame are closer to the real door's painted richness; B is a slightly flatter, smaller version of the same idea.
A is built like a solid real folding chair with chunky rounded tubes and soft lighting like the real card; B's thin wire frame has a floating back and odd joints, even though its outline is closer.
B's navy-and-gold tube on a wooden tripod uses a consistent, soft, saturated palette like the binoculars and rocking chair; A mixes white, grey and orange parts and looks more like a toy.
A's simple slab top on a plain square pedestal with stump-like stools matches how the real stone table is built; B's ornate baluster bases look too classical.
